catholic-encyclopedia-1913-alb:
Alb, a white linen vestment, has close-fitting sleeves falling nearly to the ground, secured by a girdle, or cincture. In the past it bore many names. Linea or tunica linea comes from its material. Poderis, tunica talaris, or simply talaris comes from reaching to the feet. Camisia comes from its shirt-like nature. Alba comes from its white colour, and alba Romana contrasts with shorter tunics favoured outside Rome. Of these, alba almost alone survives.

Medieval writers also use alb, plural albae, for the white garments newly baptized persons assumed on Holy Saturday. They wore them until Low Sunday, consequently known as dominica in albis, the Sunday of laying aside the white garments. Low Sunday and Trinity Sunday, with preceding days, seem sometimes to have been called Albae.
